Short answer
- From your saved catalog I found one candidate labeled "Meadowlight Lamp." I don’t have specification or source details for it in memory, so I can’t confirm energy, lumen or certification claims yet — those must be verified with the product page or manufacturer.
- If you want a practical, energy-efficient office lamp right away, choose an LED task lamp that meets the criteria below (ENERGY STAR if available, high efficacy, dimmable, tunable CCT, good CRI, and optional occupancy/auto-off). I list why each criterion matters, what to verify for any specific lamp, and a quick example of expected savings.

What I found in your catalog
- Search results: “adjustable desk lamps”, “lighting products”, “task lamps”, and one item named “Meadowlight Lamp.”
- Provenance note: I tried to fetch provenance for the Meadowlight Lamp but there are no source/extractor records in memory — so the item is present in the catalog but I have no stored specs or vendor info. That means any claims about Meadowlight (power, lumens, certification, warranty, price) require verification from the catalog entry or vendor.

Recommended lamp characteristics (and why)
1) LED light source (high efficacy)
   - Evidence: LEDs produce far more lumens per watt than incandescent or halogen. That translates directly into lower electricity use for the same light level.
   - What to verify: lumen output (lm), wattage (W), and lm/W (efficacy). Look for ~80–120 lm/W or better for best efficiency.

2) ENERGY STAR or equivalent certification (if available)
   - Evidence: ENERGY STAR/other programs test lamps for efficiency and performance.
   - What to verify: whether the specific model is listed on ENERGY STAR or a recognized regional program.

3) Dimmable + controls (manual dim, presets, or app)
   - Evidence: dimming reduces power consumption when you don’t need full output; smart controls enable schedules, occupancy settings, and further savings.
   - What to verify: true dimming (not just “levels”), whether dimming is PWM or TRIAC and whether it’s compatible with your control system.

4) Tunable color temperature (CCT) and high CRI
   - Evidence: tunable CCT (2700–6500 K) lets users select warm or cool light for comfort and focus; CRI ≥ 80–90 improves color rendering and reduces eye strain for desk tasks.
   - What to verify: CCT range and CRI rating (CRI 90+ for color-critical work).

5) Task-focused design and adjustability
   - Evidence: adjustable arms, beam control, and targeted lighting mean less stray light and more usable light on the work surface — you can use lower total output and still have good task illumination.
   - What to verify: reach/arm geometry, beam angle, and whether diffuser/optics provide even task lighting.

6) Occupancy sensor / auto-off
   - Evidence: sensors and timers reduce wasted on-time in shared spaces or when people forget to turn lights off.
   - What to verify: sensor type (PIR, ultrasonic), detection range, and user-adjustable timeout.

7) Power features (USB-A/C or wireless charging)
   - Evidence: integrated charging doesn’t save lighting energy but can reduce the need for separate chargers and improve desk ergonomics.
   - What to verify: power output (W) and charging standards (PD 18–60W, Qi spec, etc.).

Example energy-savings estimate (simple)
- If a desk lamp provides ~1,000 lm and you choose an LED that uses 10–12 W (typical for 100 lm/W), versus a 60 W incandescent producing similar perceived light, the LED uses ~80–85% less electricity. This is an estimate — check actual lumen and wattage specs for accurate savings.

Which claims need verification for any specific product (including Meadowlight Lamp)
- Exact wattage and lumen output (to compute energy use)
- lm/W efficacy
- ENERGY STAR (or similar) certification
- CRI and CCT range
- Dimming compatibility and type
- Presence and settings of occupancy sensors or timers
- Warranty, expected lifetime (e.g., 25,000–50,000 hours), and replacement/driver availability
- Price, availability, and any bundled installation costs

Next steps I can do for you
- If you want, I can:
  - Pull full specs for the Meadowlight Lamp (if you give me a link or the catalog entry ID) and verify the items above.
  - Suggest specific, proven models (brand + model) available broadly and show their specs and certifications (I’ll mark any claims I can’t verify).
  - Build a short purchasing checklist you can use to evaluate multiple lamps.

Which would you like me to do next? Also tell me your budget, desk size, preferred features (e.g., USB-C charging, smart controls, occupancy sensor), and whether you need many units for an entire office.
